summary: Firefox’s media backends received a broad round of reliability and compatibility work across Linux and Android. On Linux, Vulkan Video hardware decoding now uses Firefox’s bundled ffvpx by default, with fixes for GPU-device handling and memory sharing; on Android, MediaCodec and FFmpeg decoding and encoding better handle supported formats, Widevine-protected audio, and configured video sizes. The updates also correct audio/video timing for AVC and HEVC in Matroska files, improve codec capability checks, and refine protected playback recovery for video streams that begin unencrypted before switching to DRM.
